I frequent the forum now at least as much as the NG. Discussion content is
not at the level that it is on the NG, but some of us old-timers should be
there (the forum), at the very least to let other passers-by know the game
is quite active. Occasionally, the tedium of flamewars makes the
(presumably) moderated forums a refreshing change.
The old forum format was a total pain (truncated posts, 75 responses per
thread maximum, yeesh). The new format is much improved, yet still glitchy.
Hopefully, they'll hash out their forum issues as time progresses, and the
admins get more familiar with it. Usenet and Google Groups, while extremely
Good and Stable, are falling out of the notice of the mainstream. As VTES'
main mode of communication becomes more ignored, drawing new players to the
game becomes more difficult. Eventually, we're all going to have to make a
grand migration off of this island...

DaveZ

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Chris Shorb wrote:

> Hi, this topic has come up before. But I would like to revisit it. NG
> I love, I love the text interface, etc. But if more disussion at
> forums, perhaps will visit more often. Comments?

Is there more discussion at the WW Forum? There might be more posting, but I
dunno if there is more discussion.

Call me an elitist ass, but really, I find usenet *soooo* much more
condusive to worthwhile discussion. Or even not worthwhile discussion that
seems worthwhile. Maybe it is the flashy interface. Maybe it is the lower
bar that encourages more yahoos. But every time I look at the forum, I'm
like, "Oh. Ok. There are a few of the same usenet folks saying smart things,
and a couple not usenet folks saying smart things, but a lot of random
yahoos saying nothing at all interesting." And 'cause there are a lot of
short posts, and you have to plow through all of them to find anything, it
is hard to follow reasonable discussion. And you get stuff, like, currently,
the first thread you hit on the main page is titled "First!", and it is 8
messages about how "I posted first!" (which is apparently an exciting
element of the standard BBS Forum culture).

I mean, yeah, here we have endless discussion of insignificant things, but
at least it is, for the most part, a coherent discussion. BBS culture and
usenet culture are two different things. And for the most part, usenet
culture comes off as much smarter. So for my money? I'd stay with usenet.

It isn't a bad thing that the Forum is there. It is great for sucking folks
in. But really, I'd think the best option is to suck people in with the
forum and then steer them here.

I thought of what might be a good solution... a best of both worlds sort of
thing. What if WW hosted an archive of only those usenet forums specific to
its products, which included a good web interface for posting, and updated
the NGs in real time like a standard newsserver does? Take the poor Google
interface and lag time out, and integrate the two into one location, at the
WW site, and you've got an excellent situation. Old-timers using Forte
Agent (or whatever) could leave their habits unchanged, and new players
would see all sorts of discussion going on. It would be unmoderated
(obviously), but highly visible, being hosted at the game owner's site.
More timid participants would be one or two clicks away from the moderated
foum. Is this sort of thing possible? I think it would be, but then I'm
no Web Admin (alas, I'm just a poor chemist)...

DaveZ
Atom Weaver

Yeah, it kind of is. I'm involved in a few other BBS Forums occasonally (one
of which tends to involve me and Andrew Davidson as allies against the
world...), and they tend to be pretty low grade, in terms of signal to
noise. The VTES Forum, while certainly less wonky (likely due to less
traffic) tends to not be that much different. But then more than anything, I
suspect that is a combination of the interface and the culture of web BBS
(that is closely tied to the culture of Instant Messaging and Text
Messaging. Those darn kids today).

> I know its

> impression. That "First" thread by william was some nut kid who happened to
> post on the new forums, and in a whole bunch of places. Childish, yes, but

Exactly. Which is what happens on web BBS systems more often than not. I
mean, yeah, I'm not going to condemn the whole system for that or anything,
but it is certainly telling that when I go specifically to check out the
Forum based on this thread, the top most thread on "new threads" is that
particular thread. Which again, is very tied into the BBS Forum culture (one
of the other BBS Forums I frequent specifically had to ban "First Post!"
messages, and making one will get you warning points, just like Flaming
folks and using naughty language).

I'm not, like, super down on BBS Forums. But I find both the interface and
culture of usenet *much* better. And I realize that BBS Forums are the
future. But it strikes me as a much better option to try and keep usenet up
rather than embracing the dumbing down of the internet.

do have a much nicer immediacy to them. But then, as a guy who uses dial up
and doesn't have the most up to date web browser, I'm totally irked by the
reload times and the "You need better Flash!" messages that I constantly run

> guess I could try use Outlook without using the adress book (which is

???

The Adress book isn't a problem. I mean, yeah, if you get a virus, it might
use your address book as a means to get e-mail addresses to send itself to,
but using the address book isn't, like, going to make you more likely to get
a virus. If you get a virus, you get a virus--the address book is not really
involved (until, ya know, you already have the virus and that virus spreads
itself by sending itself to everyone in your address book) any more than,
like, using a computer is involved.

I mean, yeah, if you don't have addresses in your address book, a virus
can't use them to propagate itself. But by the same token, if you don't use
a computer, the virus can't use it to propagate itself.

Just don't get a virus. Don't open files randomly tacked on to e-mail. Get a
good virus blocker.

carry "payload" in the form of either viruses or opening up security vulnerability on your
computer so offsite users can use your computer for whatever. Most trojans look in any
number of types of files, just to find e-mail addresses. E-mail addresses are very easy to
find, just look for the @ symbol. Anyway, this was a long winded way of saying that not
using Outlook Expresses address book function will not prevent your computer from hosting
viruses or trojans.

I use Netscape Communicator 4.1 for my newsreader and e-mail program. All my in coming
POP3 mail is filtered by Norton. Also consider using anti-sypware stuff. I like Adaware
and the resources found here: <http://aumha.org/a/parasite.htm>

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Henrik Klippstr?m wrote:

> I know all of this. My point was: no adresses in adressbook = viruses
> (that spread by sending itself to all adresses in adressbook) that you
> HAPPEN to get (in spite of counterefforts) cannot spread.

I mean, yeah, I suppose, but it seems likely that any virus that wants to
find e-mail adresses is going to find them, address book or no. It just
strikes me as kind of wonky to not use an address book 'cause you might get
a virus that might use it to propagate itself. But, ya know, me.

I guess my point is that the virus issue isn't really a problem with Outlook
or the address book function so much as a problem with the world, and using
Outlook or its adress book isn't making you more vulnerable to viruses than
any other internet program.

> My other point is that I can´t see any solid arguments for not using
> forums instead of NG. IMHO!

That's easy:
A) Formus have a much klunkier interface. They are slower as they reload,
you have to fight through pointless flash adds and unecessary graphics. If
you don't have a cable modem, they are *much* slower.

B) Forums tend to be infected by the same culture as instant messaging and
text messaging--people are much more likely to respond with short, pointless
messages and not even attempt to spell/write in a coherent fashion.

Point (A) is a significant, concrete issue. Yeah, if you have the super
latest web browser and a cable modem, the reloading delays and flash adds
loading and whatever is a minimal issue, but still an issue--it still takes
time for the images to load, where with a nice, sleek text based newsreader,
none of this comes up, as it isn't necessary. Even with a cable modem, the
interface is still goofy--you have those little boxes to write in, short,
pointless messages tend to take up as much visual space as medium sized
coherent messages. Lots of flashy lights, bells, and whisltes that look
nice, but degrade the actual functional use of the system.

Point (B) is kind of an abstract issue that might not even be something that
many people notice, but if you notice it, it is annoying. People tend to
interact with Web Forums like they do with Instant Messagers--they tend to
use silly, unecessary contractions and completely ignore even remotely
coherent language structure. I mean, sure, not everyone, but enough that it
is irritating. Usenet has an established culture, mostly of, "You are
writing an article or a response to an article for people to read and
respond to. You should try and be coherent.", which is a far more satisfying
environment to have discussions in. Yeah, sometimes Usenet has flame wars,
but at least they are coherent flame wars, where Web Forums tend to have
just as many flame wars, but far less articulate flame wars.

I mean, yeah, none of this may be a bother to you (or anyone, for that
matter), but they are both significant reasons *not* to want to use a Web
Forum as opposed to Usenet.

>> My other point is that I can´t see any solid arguments for not using

Some forums I really dislike as they are just painful to read. The old WW
forums were certainly that way with no visual structure to segregate topics
enough. The Path of Blood's forums are easily managed. I'm not sure how many
forums can get away with breaking up threads into topic groups while having
enough activity in each group, but it solves to a high degree having topics can
pushed back so far that you forget about them. I recall forums like the old
"Boston" one breaking things up into groups as well, but I don't recall the
same level of activity in every group.

The new V:TES forum looks fairly standard, better than the old. If I could
only get something there I couldn't elsewhere, it would probably be tolerable,
but I'm not aware of that being the case.

With the newsgroup, to an extent, you can not keep up with it for a while and
come back and have all of the posts in front of you (at least with my newsgroup
reader). Leave an active forum too long and you lose interesting threads.

>B) Forums tend to be infected by the same culture as instant messaging and
>text messaging--people are much more likely to respond with short, pointless
>messages and not even attempt to spell/write in a coherent fashion.

I don't see the obvious difference to the newsgroup, only that such trivial
messages are easier to process with the newsgroup.

I see the biggest difference being that this newsgroup is so well established.
People interested in content will tend to congregate. If I thought there was
some source of wisdom clearly superior, I'd probably spend more time there than
here.

Roughly, I see the newsgroup having the best content but having the drawbacks
of contentiousness and the "depth"* of nonsubstantive posts.

* Probably get as many trivial posts wherever you are, but the newsgroup is
much more prone to the 300 post thread that got completely sidetracked that
will be filled with people restating their positions or otherwise not adding
anything useful. With most forums, people eventually give up on pointless
debate.

Yahoogroup, though I've only checked in on occasion rather than ever being a
member, has the advantage that the messages go right into e-mail. Seriously, I
consider this an advantage. It's much easier to keep a dialogue up when you
don't have to hunt for posts. But, it has always appeared to me to be a lot
like the newsgroup in content only dumbed down to a degree.

There are times I've preferred The Path of Blood as it seemed to have the
content and lose a lot of the noise. Then, there are times I get frustrated by
certain people who frequent it and would rather read the newsgroup or hope for
a local conversation. It clearly "wins" among forums.

Forums, not just V:TES, tend to have a problem with drawing mainly from certain
groups of players. The regional bias (as pretty much every region has one)
influences the entire forum and discussion that challenges that bias can get
crowded out.

A similar effect can happen when you get forum leaders. Often, forum leaders
end up being people who post *a lot*. Okay, there's not necessarily a problem
with that if for no other reason that someone will always be in the post lead.
But, what's the correlation between number of posts and insight? Too often,
I've seen a really smart player of a CCG who barely comments and may get
disgusted by the forum and leave. It's so frustrating to not be able to bring
together all of the top players or to not be able to at least review their
thoughts when they have their secret discussions (the last being the case with
one CCG I played).

The newsgroup seems to be more oriented towards personalities than leaders,
seems to tend towards a more heterogeneous style.

Again, it's not that forums necessarily lack diversity of thought, it's that
they often favor one sort over another due to a form of exclusivity.

Having said that, my perfect forum (in the general sense of any public
discourse) would have exclusivity ... and diversity and probably most difficult
to achieve after getting the first two - activity. Even if it means I can't
post to it. I would love to see top players and theoreticians do nothing but
hardcore analysis without the useless flames, the fluff posts, the funny posts,
tournament announcements (which can be handled elsewhere), rules questions
answered (though with certain rules discussion when a ruling is tricky). I'm
much more interested in discovering something than trying to argue my position
on something.

It's not impossible. We had at least one playtest list that worked that way,
though I would have preferred more activity, like far more decklists posted
especially during playtesting. I think how these forums come about and having
a forum be really good involves the posters respecting each other.
Disagreement is fine since the source may be regional metagames (which serious
players are trying to eliminate by sharing analysis) or simply a tentative
disagreement pending an opportunity to test a theory or having someone provide
evidence for a view. Rather than the usual "I disagree with you, therefore you
are a dumbass" take that one often sees, you might get the "why do we disagree?
let me try out your theory/deck and give you feedback on my results" Holy Grail
of analysis. Not that people have time to analyze everything under the Sun,
especially not with V:TES, where also analysis might not matter much anyway.

still less klunky than Web Forums, 'cause not only do you have HTML text and
whatever, but you also have the attractive, yet unecessary graphics and
images and whatever. It slows things down. Yeah, not a lot, but for my
money, I'm here for the text, and the extra flashy graphics and bells and
whistles (graphic smilies, personal avatar images, whatever) are just added
hinderance.
